chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from Aban ibn 'Uthman from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his hunting dog, and it caught prey, and then ate from the prey; should I eat from its remainder? He said: 'Eat what the dog killed if you recited the name [of God]; if you were forgetful, then eat from it as well, and eat from its remainder.'

key_terms.فَضْلٌ: Remainder or surplus (specifically the part eaten by the dog)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating prey caught by a hunting dog if the hunter forgot to say Bismillah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of consuming game caught by a hunting dog, emphasizing that the recitation of God's name (*tasmiyah*) is the primary condition for validity. The ruling is notably lenient, allowing consumption even if the recitation was forgotten, and explicitly permits the hunter to eat from the portion already consumed by the dog, reflecting the Shia juristic view of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in the animal's prior purity. This hadith serves as a foundational text for the rules of *sabieh* (hunting) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing it from the stricter requirements often found in Sunni schools regarding the explicit naming of God at the moment of the kill.
